summary.text: The troposphere is the lowest layer of Earth's atmosphere and the place where most weather happens.
It holds 80% of the atmosphere's mass and 99% of its water vapor and aerosols.
Heated from the surface below, it gets colder with altitude, on average by about 6.5 °C for every kilometer you climb.

facts.label: Tallest and shortest
facts.value: 18 km in tropics, 6 km in polar winter

items.prompt: You hike from a sea-level beach to the top of a 3 km mountain. Roughly how much colder should the air be at the summit?

options.label: About 2 °C colder
About 20 °C colder
About 50 °C colder
No colder at all

items.explain: Temperature falls by about 6.5 °C per kilometer on average, so 3 km of climbing means roughly 20 °C of cooling.

items.prompt: Over which part of the globe does the troposphere reach highest?

options.label: Over the poles
Over the mid-latitudes
Over the tropics
The same everywhere

items.explain: Surplus heating in the tropics expands the layer upward, to about 18 km there versus about 6 km over the poles in winter.

items.prompt: Why is air near the ground usually warmer than air a few kilometers up?

options.label: The ground soaks up sunlight and heats the air
Higher air sits closer to cold outer space
Wind carries warmth down from above
Clouds trap cold air at higher levels

items.explain: The surface absorbs most of the Sun's energy and then heats the troposphere from below.

items.prompt: A pocket of dry air is pushed up a mountainside without gaining or losing heat. Why does it still cool down?

options.label: Higher up, the Sun's rays are weaker
It mixes with icy air from above
It loses its water vapor as it climbs
It expands and spends energy pushing outward

items.explain: Lower pressure lets the rising parcel expand; pushing against the surrounding air uses up its energy, which shows up as a drop in temperature.

items.prompt: A rising bubble of air reaches a new height and finds itself colder than the air around it. What does it do next?

options.label: Speeds up and keeps rising
Sinks back toward where it started
Spreads sideways and stays put
Warms up instantly to match

items.explain: Being colder, the parcel is denser than its surroundings, so it falls back to its original height: the air is stable against lifting.

items.prompt: Nearly all clouds and rain form in the lowest layer of the atmosphere. Which fact about that layer explains this best?

options.label: It has the most argon of any layer
Its temperature never changes with height
It holds almost all the air's water vapor
It is the thinnest layer of the atmosphere

items.explain: The troposphere contains 99% of the atmosphere's water vapor, and it is where most weather happens.
